subject: Acuvera dedicated capacity: sizing profile & surge runway
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acuvera dedicated capacity: sizing profile & surge runway

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discovery, Acuvera expects a bursty clinical-annotation workload (patient message summarization + triage prompts) with the following initial/pivot assumptions:

- Peak concurrent requests: ~220 rps (inbound API calls) during morning surge windows (08:00–10:30 local).
- Typical request length: model prompts + history ≈ 1.8k tokens in, ~300 tokens generated on average.
- SLO: 95% of requests < 350ms p95 for interactive triage flows; background batch jobs can accept higher latency.
- Target start date for dedicated: 2026-04-01, trial month followed by reserved commit.

To move sizing forward we need: a realistic token/sec profile (per-minute buckets if possible), any quiet-hours attenuation factors, and the MOP (procurement contact + billing cadence). Can you share an export or a short traffic sample? If you prefer, the attached spreadsheet shows our minimal inputs for a quick TD estimate.

Next actions I propose:
1) You send a small traffic sample or confirm the per-minute peak in the attached template.
2) Marissa will do a tokens/sec -> GPU slab sketch and return a conservative headroom calc.
3) Jordan will prepare the draft mutual action plan and procurement checklist for your team.

Thanks — happy to hop on another 30-min sync if helpful.

Best,
Karthik Iyer

I’ve cc’d procurement for contract milestones and to confirm billing cadence (monthly preferred). Let us know if the sample format works.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Samantha Tan <samantha.tan@acuvera.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acuvera dedicated capacity: sizing profile & surge runway

Thanks for the data, Samantha — did a quick pass and sketched a conservative GPU mapping so we can align on SLAs. High-level notes (rough sketch for discussion):

- Observed peak tokens/sec (estimate): 230 rps * (1750 + 320) tokens/request ≈ 470k tokens/sec (aggregate peak).
- Using our internal throughput baseline (A100-equivalent slab @ 1.3M tokens/sec for 8-bit quantized encoder-decoder char-RL model with KV cache warmed) — a single slab can handle ~1.3M t/s baseline but tail latency increases with concurrency.
- For p95 < 350ms target: we recommend starting with a 0.5x conservative factor to account for cold-starts, prefix variability, and networking: effective pick = 1.3M * 0.5 ≈ 650k t/s per slab at target latency.
- Mapping → 470k/650k ≈ 0.72 slabs; recommend reserving 1 full slab for production, plus a 40% headroom buffer to absorb short surges and model variance → 1.4 slabs. Practically that maps to reserving 2 slabs (dedicated GPUs) for the initial commit.

Operational suggestions:
- Autoscale burst policy: enable short-lived burst credits (30–60s) to permit spikes to 2.5x for very short windows; this avoids persistent overcommit.
- KV cache warmup: pre-warm common patient-history prefixes during morning run to avoid tail p99 spikes.
- Canary: run a canary of 10% traffic on dedicated then roll to 100% over 24–48 hours.

Open items for accurate pricing/commit:
1) Clarify model family (LLM variant) — we used a conservative A100-equivalent baseline. If you plan a smaller/faster model we can shift to 1-slab starting.
2) Confirm expected growth: monthly token increase or expected change in peak windows.
3) Procurement preference on burst billing (metered vs. included burst pool).

I’ll attach a short PDF with the math and the slab-to-cost delta for a 12-month commit.

—Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: karthik_sizing_notes_v1.pdf (calculation summary)

Hello —

Procurement here. A couple items to flag before we sign:
- We need an explicit SLA clause for p95 latency for triage endpoints and the definition of a failed request (timeout vs. degraded content).
- Please provide a proposed pricing table showing: 1) baseline reserved slabs, 2) burst credits pricing, 3) overage rates beyond reserved commit.
- For security review: confirm whether logs/audit trails can be routed to our S3 KMS and the retention period options.

If you can provide a short redline-ready term sheet with those items, we can circulate internally this week.

Thanks,
Acuvera Procurement
procurement@acuvera.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acuvera dedicated capacity: sizing profile & surge runway

Hi all —

Quick follow to address procurement asks and lock a pragmatic commitment shape:

1) SLA language: we can offer a targeted p95 SLA for the triage route at 350ms with a 99.9% availability target for the dedicated service. SLA credits are tiered and tied specifically to the triage endpoint identifier. I’ll circulate the specific clause as a DocuSign link by EOD.

2) Pricing table (high level):
- Reserved (monthly): 2 slabs @ $XX,XXX per slab (12-month commit pricing in the attached draft).
- Burst credits: first 10 minutes/day included in commit; additional metered burst billed at $Y per 1M tokens beyond commit.
- Overage: automatically metered hourly if sustained above the commit for > 10 minutes, capped at a 3x multiplier.

3) Security/logs: dedicated can ship audit logs to your S3 with customer KMS; retention windows 30/90/365 days configurable. We’ll include required SOC2 attestation references and a short runbook for log handoff.

Next steps: Jordan will share a one-page mutual action plan and a draft term sheet. If Acuvera signs off on 2 reserved slabs + the burst pool, we can schedule a provisioning window (2–3 business days) and the canary cutover.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success (Enterprise), Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
